results.diagnosis: The add function is using subtraction operator (-) instead of addition operator (+).
The function forgot to divide discount_percent by 100 to convert it from a percentage value to a decimal multiplier.
The function uses > 60 instead of >= 60, causing a score of exactly 60 to be marked as failing when it should pass.
The function reverses the entire string character-by-character instead of reversing the order of words in the sentence.
The function uses range(n) which produces 0 to n-1, but should use range(1, n+1) to sum from 1 to n inclusive as expected by the test.
Mutable default argument causes the list to persist across function calls, accumulating items from previous invocations.
The function does not convert words to lowercase before counting, treating different case variations of the same word as separate entries.

The base case condition only checks for n == 1, but factorial(0) should also return 1 (since 0! = 1). When factorial(0) is called, it doesn't match the base case and recurses infinitely into negative numbers, causing a RecursionError.
The function does not handle division by zero, which should return 0 instead of raising a ZeroDivisionError.
The parse_age function does not handle invalid input (non-numeric strings and None values) and should return 0 for these cases instead of raising exceptions.
The function uses wrong index `len(items)` instead of `len(items) - 1` (off by one error) to access the last element, and doesn't handle empty lists.
The function uses direct dictionary access which raises a KeyError when the 'email' key is missing, but it should return None instead.
The function uses union operator (|) instead of intersection operator (&) to find common elements between two lists.
The function converts the username to lowercase but fails to strip leading and trailing whitespace before doing so.
The base case for the factorial recursion is checking for n == 1 instead of n == 0, causing factorial(0) to recurse infinitely into negative numbers.
The while loop condition is `low < high` instead of `low <= high`, preventing the algorithm from checking the element when low and high converge to the same index.
The function crashes with ZeroDivisionError when given an empty list because it attempts to divide by zero instead of checking if the list is empty and returning 0.
The function doesn't convert the text to lowercase before checking for buzzwords, so uppercase or mixed-case buzzwords won't be detected.
